Home / Museum Ship Reports / Emden Guns – Sydney/Canberra

Location 1: Hyde Park, College St, Darlinghurst, NSW 2010, Australia

Location 2: HMAS Kuttabul Garden Island Precinct, Wylde St, Potts Point, NSW 2011, Australia

Location 3: Australian War Memorial, Treloar Cres, Campbell, ACT 2612, Australia

Visited: Various

On 9 November 1914, the German cruiser Emden was engaged and sunk by the Australian light cruiser HMAS Sydney (I) near the Cocos (Keeling) Islands. In 1917 one of the 4.1-inch guns recovered from Emden was erected in Hyde Park in Sydney as a memorial to the battle, near the present site of the ANZAC war memorial.

There is a second Emden gun in Sydney, mounted on Garden Island near the former site of the RAN Heritage Centre - where it has a direct line of sight to the signal mast of HMAS Sydney (I) - erected across the harbour at Bradley Head.

A third gun from Emden is on display at the Australian War Memorial in Canberra.
